title: What's Included on a Nile Cruise? Full Breakdown
excerpt: What's included on a Nile cruise: full-board cabin, licensed Egyptologist, sightseeing with entrance fees, transfers. Drinks and tips are extra. From €610.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

On the Nile cruise packages Sawa lists, the price includes your cabin on full board, a licensed Egyptologist guide, the guided sightseeing and entrance fees named in the itinerary, and airport meet-and-assist with transfers. Drinks, tips, optional excursions, special tombs, travel insurance and international flights are extra. "Full board" means all meals, not all drinks. The lists below follow those on the live Nile Majesty package page as of 8 November 2026; always read the lists on the exact package you book.

UNESCO documents the temples and necropolis of ancient Thebes, including Luxor and its West Bank.

Key facts

Fact Detail

Nile cruise listings love the phrase "all-inclusive", and travellers reasonably assume it covers everything from sunscreen to cocktails. It almost never does. The honest way to compare cruises is to read two lists, included and excluded, on the package you are actually booking. This guide follows both lists from a live Sawa package, the Nile Majesty 5-day cruise from Luxor, so you can see where the price stops and your wallet starts. It is written by the team behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), founded by a guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, and we publish these lists on every cruise page for precisely this reason.

What's included: the list, from a live cruise

The Nile Majesty package (5 days, Luxor to Aswan, from €610 per person, as listed in November 2026) includes four bundles:

  • The cabin and board. Four nights aboard a five-star Nile cruiser on full board: meals on board for the length of the cruise.
  • The guiding. A licensed Egyptologist guide, one guide for your group of up to eight rather than a new one at every dock. The ship is shared with other guests; your group does the excursions together with its guide.
  • The sightseeing. Guided sightseeing and entrance fees listed in the itinerary: Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, the Temple of Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon, Luxor Temple on an evening horse-drawn carriage ride, Edfu and Kom Ombo, Philae and the Aswan High Dam. The standard entrance ticket for each of those stops is covered; special tombs in the Valley of the Kings, such as Tutankhamun's, are never included.
  • The edges. Meet-and-assist at Luxor and Aswan airports, the horse-drawn carriage ride in Luxor, and felucca sailing in Aswan, including an evening around Kitchener's Island.

Read that list against any competitor's cruise: if theirs does not name the excursions, the entrance fees and the board basis as plainly, the missing lines are where the extras will appear.

What's not included: drinks, tips and the extras

The not-included list is equally explicit, and it is worth reading slowly: "International flights"; "Travel insurance"; "Drinks and personal expenses"; "Optional excursions outside the itinerary"; and "Tipping and gratuities".

Two of those surprise travellers more than the rest. Full board is not all-inclusive: your meals on board are covered, but drinks are not. And tipping sits outside the price. Cruise ships typically run a pooled tip box for the crew, with the guide and driver tipped separately; 2026 guides quote about US$5 to 15 per person per night for the crew (about €4 to €13), and amounts vary, so ask at reception how the ship handles it. Optional excursions beyond the itinerary (a hot-air balloon ride is not in Sawa's day tours but is optional on some packages, such as Egypt in Depth), your visa and your international flights round out the budget; check Egypt's official e-visa portal before you fly.

How it varies, and what to check before booking

Inclusions shift between packages, so the lists on whichever page you book are the ones that govern. Sawa's own cruise range shows how. The Nile Discovery 4-day runs Aswan to Luxor over three nights from €500, with an Egyptologist guide, and also lists bottled water during excursions, the domestic flight from Luxor to Cairo and a Nile dinner cruise in Cairo; it lists tips for guides, cruise staff and drivers as optional and not included. The 9-day Egypt in Depth adds four Cairo hotel nights and domestic flights to a four-night cruise, in three comfort tiers, from €1,403, with meals counted separately (eight breakfasts, five lunches and seven dinners over the nine days). All prices are per person, as listed in November 2026, and fixed per traveller. All-inclusive drinks packages exist elsewhere in the market: compare like with like.

Before paying, check three lines on any listing: the drinks line, the tipping line, and the named excursion list. Then read the payment side. Reserving a seat on a forming date is free and nothing is charged until four travellers have reserved it. On a cruise package, a 25% deposit is due at the GoAhead and the balance 14 days before departure, and a date must reach four by 30 days before. Cancel 30 or more days out at no charge; from 29 to 15 days you lose half the deposit (12.5%); at 14 days or fewer, or a no-show, the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as flights or cabins, may become non-refundable earlier, and that is disclosed before you pay. The full schedule is in Sawa's terms. For how the confirmation works, see how the GoAhead works.

How to book the Nile Majesty cruise with Sawa

The Nile Majesty: 5-Day River Cruise from Luxor runs Luxor to Aswan with the lists above, departing Mondays and Saturdays, from €610 per person, as listed in November 2026. Shared departures run four to eight travellers. You reserve a seat on a forming date free; when four travellers have reserved it, the date reaches the GoAhead and is confirmed to run, and only then is the 25% deposit charged, by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. If a date has not reached four by 30 days before departure, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested. A solo cabin is confirmed in the booking, so check it before you pay. Browse the forming and confirmed departures, read the FAQ, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613, answered 24/7 while your tour is running.

The short version

A Nile cruise price buys the cabin on full board, the Egyptologist, every guided excursion and entrance fee in the itinerary, and the airport transfers; it does not buy drinks, tips, optional extras or your international flights. The Nile Majesty 5-day cruise publishes both lists, from €610 per person, as listed in November 2026, confirmed at four travellers. The best cruise listings answer this page before you ask it. Reserve free on the forming departures, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613.

faq.a: Usually no. Most Nile cruises, including the five-star ships on Sawa's packages, are full board: meals included, drinks not. All-inclusive drinks packages exist in the market, but treat the two words as separate claims and check the inclusions list on the exact package before comparing prices.

faq.q: Are drinks included on a Nile cruise?
faq.a: On the Nile Majesty departure, no: "Drinks and personal expenses" sit in the not-included list (checked 8 November 2026). Paid soft drinks, water bottles and bar orders go on your onboard account, so budget for drinks and personal spending separately. Nile Discovery lists bottled water during excursions as included, which is a different arrangement from drinks on the ship.

faq.q: Are excursions and entrance fees included on a Nile cruise?
faq.a: On the Sawa cruises we checked, yes: guided sightseeing and entrance fees listed in the itinerary are an explicit inclusion, covering Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut, Edfu, Kom Ombo, Philae and the High Dam on the Nile Majesty, with a licensed Egyptologist guide. Special tombs, such as Tutankhamun's, and excursions outside the printed itinerary are priced separately.

faq.q: How much should I tip on a Nile cruise?
faq.a: Tipping is excluded from the package price and is customary in Egypt. Cruises typically run a pooled tip box for the crew, handed to reception in an envelope on the last evening, with separate tips for the guide and driver; bring small notes. Guides in 2026 quote about US$5 to 15 per person per night for the crew, and the amounts vary, so ask on board rather than guessing.
